compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Once a store actually syncs more than one tracker project, an older rebar binary reading it is
dangerous rather than merely limited: it would fetch only its single configured project, see every
other project's bound tickets as having no corresponding remote issue, and create duplicate issues in
the wrong project. There is a shipped mechanism for exactly this — `.store-compat.json` with a
fail-closed read (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`) — but `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` is still an empty frozenset
(`compat.py:60`), so no capability has ever been declared through it.

## Approach

Register `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. That single addition is what makes a binary
able to *recognise* the capability; a binary that predates it hits the "required capability this
binary does not provide" branch and raises `StoreIncompatibleError`, refusing writes rather than
corrupting the store (`docs/migrations.md:158-165`).

This is the expand half of the expand/contract rollout `docs/migrations.md:138-149` describes: teach
binaries to read and fail closed **before** anything writes the requirement. Registering the name here
is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story, so shipping it changes no behaviour for any
existing store. The conditional stamp lands separately, which is why the two are ordered rather than
combined.

Reads deliberately stay available: the gate is on the write lock only
(`docs/migrations.md:174-178`), so `list`/`show`/`search` keep working against a store an old binary
may not write, and `fsck` surfaces the condition as a structured `compat_error` without changing its
exit code.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's pure-branch row: an in-process unit test against the real
classification function, since the mechanism is entirely a validation branch with no I/O of its own —
plus one real-store test for the write-gate, because the gate fires inside lock acquisition and a
unit test would not cross that component.

- Happy path: a record declaring `multi-project-bridge` classifies as compatible on a binary that
  registers it.
- Contrast case: a record declaring an unregistered capability name still raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError` — proving the registration widened the known set by exactly one entry and
  did not disable the check.
- Absent-record regression: a store with no `.store-compat.json` still passes through as implicit
  legacy, so pre-feature stores are unaffected.
- Write-gate path: a store whose record declares an unknown capability refuses a write through the
  real lock acquisition, while `list`/`show` against the same store still succeed. The read half is
  the contrast case that proves the gate is scoped to writes.
- Corrupt-record path: a malformed record still raises rather than being treated as absent, which is
  the bypass the gate is designed to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `multi-project-bridge` is in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` and a record declaring it classifies as
      compatible; checked by a unit test over the classification function.
- [ ] A record declaring an unregistered capability still raises `StoreIncompatibleError`; checked by
      the paired negative case.
- [ ] A store with no compat record still passes through as implicit legacy; checked by an
      absent-record regression test.
- [ ] A store declaring an unknown capability refuses writes while reads still succeed; checked by a
      real-store test exercising the write lock and a read command against the same store.
- [ ] A corrupt record raises rather than being treated as absent; checked by a malformed-record test.
